definition: A training strategy that presents training examples to a model in a meaningful order, typically progressing from easier to harder examples.
details: Curriculum learning is inspired by how humans often learn, and has been shown in some settings to speed up training convergence and improve final model performance.

explainer.lead: Curriculum learning trains a model on examples in a meaningful order, usually starting with easier cases and moving toward harder ones. Borrowing an idea from human education, this ordering can sometimes help training converge faster or produce a better final model.

tiers.eli5: It is like learning addition before trying algebra, rather than seeing every kind of math problem mixed together from the start. A model begins with simple examples and gradually gets harder ones. In some cases, this helps it learn faster or do better in the end.
tiers.practitioner: Define a difficulty measure, construct an easy-to-hard data schedule, and train with the usual model and objective. Compare convergence and final performance against randomly shuffled training, because the benefit is setting-dependent and a poor difficulty measure can undermine the schedule.
tiers.paperLevel: Given D = {(x_i, y_i)}, assign each example a difficulty score s_i and train on a sequence of subsets or batches D_1, ..., D_T whose examples generally progress from lower to higher s_i. The schedule changes data presentation rather than the learning objective; improvements in convergence or final performance are empirical and are not guaranteed.

explainer.example: To train a model on arithmetic, begin with single-digit addition, move to multi-digit addition, and finish with multi-step word problems, while using the same model throughout.

usedIn.name: Machine learning
usedIn.detail: Training examples can be scheduled by estimated difficulty instead of being presented in an arbitrary order.

usedIn.name: Neural network training
usedIn.detail: Easy-to-hard batches can be used while keeping the network and training objective unchanged.

explainer.intuition: Early easy examples can establish basic patterns before the model faces more complicated cases, much as foundational lessons prepare a person for advanced material.
howItWorks: Choose a way to estimate each example's difficulty.
Arrange examples or batches from easier to harder.
Train the model through that schedule.
explainer.whyItMatters: Changing only the order of training data can sometimes speed up convergence and improve final performance, without requiring a different task or learning objective.
misconceptions: It does not guarantee faster or better training.
It need not use one strict, permanent ordering.
It changes data presentation, not the task itself.
